name: Language
description: How a file is read for what a person put in it.

text: Which language reads a file for what a person wrote is the same
question as which files a reading reaches, so it is asked once: a
mechanism scans everything its globs cover, and a language claiming
nothing is how a file is passed over. Reading it for what it declares
is a different question — a name is spelled the way one language
spells it — so there the language arrives named.
No mechanism names a language. The one answering owns the shapes
it hands back — those more than one language would answer with —
which is why a region of prose lives here and a name's parameters
stay with the reading that makes them.

scenarios.title: What a person wrote in a source file
given: a Ruby file carrying comments and identifiers
scenarios.when: the file is read for what a person wrote
scenarios.then: the comments answer and nothing else does

scenarios.title: A file no language claims
scenarios.when: the file is read for what a person wrote

scenarios.title: Nowhere for a claim to sit
scenarios.when: the file is read for where a claim could sit

scenarios.title: The language a specification named is the one that reads it
given: a specification naming the language it is written in
scenarios.when: the file is read for what it declares
scenarios.then: that language answers, rather than the one the filename implies

scenarios.title: Depth is not a barrier
given: a Ruby file whose claims sit in a class body, a method body and a block comment
scenarios.when: the file is read for where a claim could sit
scenarios.then: all of them answer, at whatever depth they sit

scenarios.title: A comment nothing follows
given: a Ruby file whose last line is a comment
scenarios.when: the file is read for where a claim could sit

scenarios.title: Source the grammar cannot read
given: a Ruby file the grammar cannot parse
scenarios.when: the file is read for where a claim could sit
scenarios.then: the file is named as unreadable rather than answering with what it recovered

scenarios.title: A language this build was not given
given: a name no language this executable carries answers to
scenarios.when: the build is asked whether it carries that language
scenarios.then: it answers that it does not, rather than reading the file some other way

scenarios.title: How a language spells what it defines
given: a name a language spells and one named the way a route is named
scenarios.when: each is put to that language
scenarios.then: only the one it could spell answers, and neither says anything is defined
